issues.legal_issue: Conferring specified telegraph-authority powers on an electricity supply licensee does not incorporate the entire telegraph statute into the electricity statute or subject all the licensee’s rights and liabilities to it.
material_facts: The company held a licence to supply electricity and had been granted specified powers of a telegraph authority to place electric supply lines and apparatus.
The dispute concerned a municipal demand for fees for land occupied by the company’s electric poles.
issues.conclusion: The grant of specified telegraph-authority powers did not incorporate the entire telegraph statute into the electricity statute or make that statute govern all the licensee’s rights and liabilities.
issues.legal_principle: Section 51 of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, empowers the State Government to confer on a licensee powers possessed by a telegraph authority under the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, for specified purposes. It does not incorporate all provisions of the Telegraph Act into the Electricity Act; the grant of some powers under the Telegraph Act does not make all the licensee’s rights and liabilities subject to that Act. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.electricity_supply_licensee: A person or company holds a licence to supply electricity.
predicates.specific_telegraph_powers_granted: The government grants the licensee specified powers that a telegraph authority possesses for placing electric supply lines or apparatus.

issues.definition: When an electricity supply licensee receives specified telegraph-authority powers, that grant does not itself import the entire telegraph law into the licensee’s legal regime.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory reference procedure limited to disputes involving a telegraph authority and specified telegraph powers cannot be treated as the required remedy for a dispute between an electricity licensee and a local authority outside those categories.
material_facts: The company disputed a local authority’s demand for fees for land occupied by its electric poles and sought relief in a constitutional writ petition.
The High Court rejected the petition solely because it considered a statutory reference procedure to be the proper remedy.
The company was an electricity licensee, not a telegraph authority, and the dispute was not one of the specified disputes covered by that procedure.
The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and remitted the case for disposal according to law, without deciding whether the company was entitled to the substantive relief it sought.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in rejecting the writ petition on the ground that the dispute had to be referred under Section 15 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885. The petition was remitted for consideration according to law, with its merits left undecided.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, applies to disputes between a telegraph authority and a local authority of the kinds specified in that section, including disputes concerning the exercise of powers conferred by the Act. A licensee under the Indian Electricity Act is not thereby a telegraph authority, and the provision does not extend to other disputes. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.writ_petition_rejected_on_reference_grou: A court rejects a constitutional writ petition solely because it considers a statutory reference procedure to be the required remedy.
predicates.dispute_between_electricity_licensee_and: An electricity supply licensee disputes a demand or action by a local authority.
predicates.licensee_not_telegraph_authority: The electricity supply licensee is not a person legally defined as a telegraph authority.
predicates.dispute_outside_enumerated_telegraph_cat: The dispute does not fall within the specified categories of disputes covered by the telegraph-related reference procedure.

issues.definition: If a writ petition about a dispute between an electricity licensee and a local authority is rejected solely on a reference ground, but the licensee is not a telegraph authority and the dispute is outside the covered categories, that ground cannot justify rejecting the petition.
